softmax: Like converting raw test scores into percentages that sum to 100% — the highest raw score gets the biggest slice, and all slices always add up to 1.
attention: Like a search engine inside the model: you have a query (what you're looking for) and it finds the most relevant words in the input to focus on.
multi-head attention: Like reading a sentence with multiple highlighters at once — one tracks grammar, one tracks meaning, one tracks coreference — and you combine all the highlights at the end.
dropout: Like a sports team that practices with random players absent each session — so every player learns the whole playbook, not just their part.
residual connections: Like a shortcut road on a highway — even if the main route is congested (gradients vanish), information can bypass layers and still reach the destination.
layer normalization: Like adjusting every instrument's volume in an orchestra so no single one drowns out the others, keeping the mix balanced.
relu: Like a one-way valve: any negative signal is blocked (becomes 0), any positive signal flows through unchanged.
backpropagation: Like tracing blame backwards through a chain of decisions — the model figures out who was responsible for the error and adjusts each part accordingly.
gradient descent: Like rolling a ball down a foggy hill — you can't see the bottom, but you always step in whichever direction feels downhill.
embedding: Like a coordinate system for words — 'king' and 'queen' end up close together, 'king' and 'banana' end up far apart.
positional encoding: Like adding timestamps to chat messages — the content doesn't change, but now you know which came first.
convolution: Like sliding a magnifying glass over a photo, looking for the same pattern (an edge, a curve) at every position.
pooling: Like summarising a paragraph into one key sentence — you lose detail but keep the essential information.
batch normalization: Like standardising exam scores to a common scale so results from different exams are directly comparable.
transformer: Like a translation office where every word can directly ask every other word for context, instead of waiting for messages to pass through a chain.
cross entropy loss: Like measuring how surprised you are by the right answer — if you were 99% confident and got it wrong, that's a massive surprise (high loss).
lstm: Like a notebook with selective memory — it actively decides what to write down, what to erase, and what to carry forward.
sigmoid: Like a dimmer switch that squashes any input to a value between 0 and 1, useful for representing yes/no probabilities.
learning rate: Like the size of your steps when walking down a hill — too big and you overshoot the bottom, too small and you take forever.
overfitting: Like memorising the practice exam word-for-word instead of understanding the topic — you ace the practice test but fail the real one.
regularization: Like penalising a student for writing an essay that's too long — it forces them to be concise and focus on what matters.
neural network: Like a chain of filters — raw input passes through each filter, and each one learns to detect increasingly abstract patterns.
dot product: Like measuring how similar two arrows are: if they point in the same direction, the result is high; if they're perpendicular, it's zero.
gradient: Like the slope of a hill at your current position — it tells you which direction is steepest, and how steep.
seq2seq: Like a telephone interpreter: they listen to the full sentence in one language before translating it into another.
